title: A bireporter recombinant SARS-CoV-2 Omicron BA.5 for in vitro and in vivo studies.
abstract: ABSTRACT The continuous emergence of variants of concern (VoCs) represents a significant challenge to effectively control severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). Although FDA-approved vaccines and antivirals have been successfully developed and implemented for the prophylactic and therapeutic intervention of SARS-CoV-2 infection, recent VoCs could escape protection garnered by previous vaccine and antiviral approaches. Determining the efficacy of prophylactics and/or therapeutics against recent VoCs will assist in efficiently controlling currently circulating SARS-CoV-2 strains. We used our previously described bacterial artificial chromosome-based reverse genetics approach for Omicron BA.5 to generate a recombinant SARS-CoV-2 BA.5 encoding a fusion of ZsGreen to Nanoluciferase (rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc) from the locus of the viral nucleocapsid (N) protein separated by the porcine teschovirus-1 2A proteolytic cleavage site. The rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc replicates to levels comparable to recombinant BA.5 wild type (rBA.5 WT) and expresses high levels of ZsG and Nluc in cultured cells. This facilitates tracking viral infection and the identification of antivirals and neutralizing antibodies with EC 50 and NT 50 values, respectively, similar to those obtained with rBA.5 WT. Importantly, in Keratin-18 human angiotensin-converting enzyme-2 mice, rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc retains the same pathogenicity and ability to replicate in the lungs of infected mice as rBA.5 WT. Using rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc, we detected Nluc activity systemically and Nluc and ZsG expression in the lungs of infected mice using an in vivo imaging system. Our results demonstrate the feasibility of using rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc to track viral infections and identify prophylactics and therapeutics against recent SARS-CoV-2 VoCs in vitro , ex vivo , and in vivo . IMPORTANCE Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), the causative virus of the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic, is continually evolving to escape immunity acquired by previous natural infections or vaccinations. Moreover, recent SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern (VoCs) have acquired antiviral-resistant mutations to FDA-approved drugs. The emergence of these VoCs highlights the importance of identifying new prophylactics and therapeutics against currently circulating SARS-CoV-2 strains. We generated a recombinant bireporter Omicron BA.5 SARS-CoV-2 (rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc) that expresses reporter proteins, which are useful for cellular and whole animal studies, and has similar viral replication and pathogenicity to a wild-type recombinant Omicron BA.5 SARS-CoV-2. In Keratin-18 human angiotensin-converting enzyme-2 mice, rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc infection can be tracked systemically or in the lungs of infected mice using an in vivo imaging system. We establish a proof-of-concept platform of rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc in combination with an ancestral SARS-CoV-2 strain expressing mCherry to simultaneously identify antivirals and neutralizing antibodies against original and recent SARS-CoV-2 strains.

source_records.title: A bireporter recombinant SARS-CoV-2 Omicron BA.5 for in vitro and in vivo studies
source_records.abstract: ABSTRACT The continuous emergence of variants of concern (VoCs) represents a significant challenge to effectively control severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). Although FDA-approved vaccines and antivirals have been successfully developed and implemented for the prophylactic and therapeutic intervention of SARS-CoV-2 infection, recent VoCs could escape protection garnered by previous vaccine and antiviral approaches. Determining the efficacy of prophylactics and/or therapeutics against recent VoCs will assist in efficiently controlling currently circulating SARS-CoV-2 strains. We used our previously described bacterial artificial chromosome-based reverse genetics approach for Omicron BA.5 to generate a recombinant SARS-CoV-2 BA.5 encoding a fusion of ZsGreen to Nanoluciferase (rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc) from the locus of the viral nucleocapsid (N) protein separated by the porcine teschovirus-1 2A proteolytic cleavage site. elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们使用之前描述的基于细菌人工染色体的反向遗传学方法生成了一种重组严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 BA.5株(rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc),该株在病毒核衣壳(N)蛋白基因位点中融合了ZsGreen和Nanoluciferase(rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc),并由猪睾丸病毒-1 2A蛋白酶切割位点分隔。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些VoCs的出现凸显了识别针对当前流行的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2株的新预防和治疗药物的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 我们生成了一种双报告基因重组奥密克戎BA.5 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2株(rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc),该株表达报告基因蛋白,适用于细胞和整体动物研究,并且其病毒复制和致病性与野生型重组奥密克戎BA.5 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2相似。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 我们建立了一个rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc与表达mCherry的祖先严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2株相结合的可行性平台,以同时识别抗病毒药物和针对原始及近期严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2株的中和抗体。

abstract_zh: 摘要 连续出现的关注变异株(VoCs)对有效控制严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2)构成了重大挑战。尽管美国食品药品监督管理局(FDA)批准的疫苗和抗病毒药物已成功开发并用于严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染的预防和治疗干预,但最近的VoCs可能逃逸先前疫苗和抗病毒药物方法提供的保护。确定现有预防和/或治疗药物对近期VoCs的效果将有助于高效控制当前流行的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2株。我们使用之前描述的基于细菌人工染色体的反向遗传学方法生成了一种重组严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 BA.5株(rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc),该株在病毒核衣壳(N)蛋白基因位点中融合了ZsGreen和Nanoluciferase(rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc),并由猪睾丸病毒-1 2A蛋白酶切割位点分隔。rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc在培养细胞中复制水平与重组BA.5野生型(rBA.5 WT)相当,并且高水平表达ZsG和Nluc。这有助于追踪病毒感染并识别抗病毒药物和中和抗体,其EC 50和NT 50值分别与使用rBA.5 WT获得的结果相似。重要的是,在角蛋白-18人血管紧张素转换酶-2小鼠中,rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc在感染小鼠肺部的复制能力和致病性与rBA.5 WT相同。利用rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc,我们通过体内成像系统检测了感染小鼠体内Nluc活性以及肺部Nluc和ZsG的表达。我们的结果表明,使用rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc可以有效地追踪病毒感染,并在体外、离体和体内环境中识别针对当前流行的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2株的预防和治疗药物。重要性 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2),即2019年冠状病毒疾病(新型冠状病毒感染)大流行的病原体,持续进化以逃逸由先前自然感染或疫苗接种获得的免疫力。此外,近期的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2关注变异株(VoCs)已获得了对FDA批准药物抗病毒药物的抗性。这些VoCs的出现凸显了识别针对当前流行的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2株的新预防和治疗药物的重要性。我们生成了一种双报告基因重组奥密克戎BA.5 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2株(rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc),该株表达报告基因蛋白,适用于细胞和整体动物研究,并且其病毒复制和致病性与野生型重组奥密克戎BA.5 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2相似。在角蛋白-18人血管紧张素转换酶-2小鼠中,利用体内成像系统可以追踪rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc感染的全身或肺部情况。我们建立了一个rBA.5 ZsG-Nluc与表达mCherry的祖先严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2株相结合的可行性平台,以同时识别抗病毒药物和针对原始及近期严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2株的中和抗体。

title: The α-helix-facilitating amino acid sequence EAAAK dramatically increases the antiviral activity of SARS-CoV-2 fusion-inhibitory peptides via the endosome fusion pathway.
abstract: UNLABELLED: The SARS-CoV-2 fusion-inhibitory lipopeptide IPB29 features a unique design incorporating the α-helix-promoting EAAAK sequence as a rigid linker between the peptide backbone and the conjugated lipid, exhibiting greatly improved antiviral activity compared to lipopeptides with conventional flexible linkers. Here, we characterized its mechanism of action and uncovered several critical insights. First, IPB29 remained the most potent inhibitor of emerging Omicron subvariants compared to IPB24 and IPB28, which share the same peptide sequence but employ flexible polyethylene glycol or glycine-serine repeat linker. Notably, this enhanced potency was abolished in Vero E6 cells stably expressing TMPRSS2, where viral entry occurs via the plasma membrane fusion pathway. Visualization using FITC-labeled lipopeptides demonstrated that IPB29 binds to and enters target cells more efficiently. Subsequently, we generated two unconjugated template peptides, P43 (containing EAAAK) and P37 (lacking EAAAK). P43 exhibited superior inhibitory activity compared to P37 in Huh-7 and 293T/ACE2 cells, but not in Vero E6-TMPRSS2 cells. Both peptides showed comparable efficacy in blocking S protein-driven cell-cell fusion. Although P43 displayed enhanced α-helicity relative to P37, both peptides exhibited similar target-binding affinities. Instead, the cellular uptake of P43 was markedly more efficient, further supporting that the improved antiviral effect is attributable to the inhibition of the viral endosomal fusion pathway. Collectively, our studies provide molecular insights into the antiviral mechanism of IPB29 and propose the short EAAAK sequence as a generalizable strategy for enhancing the efficacy of peptide-based therapeutics. IMPORTANCE: The development of effective therapeutics against SARS-CoV-2 remains an urgent priority. IPB29, a potent broad-spectrum lipopeptide fusion inhibitor currently in clinical trials, requires mechanistic elucidation. Here, we demonstrate that the C-terminal EAAAK motif in IPB29-originally designed as a rigid linker connecting the peptide backbone to the lipid moiety-is critical for its antiviral activity and functions via the endosomal fusion pathway. These findings reveal a generalizable strategy for optimizing antiviral drug design.

The background highlights the urgent need for effective therapeutics against SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study characterized the mechanism of action of IPB29 and compared its antiviral activity with other lipopeptides, including IPB24 and IPB28, in different cell lines such as Huh-7, 293T/ACE2, and Vero E6-TMPRSS2 cells.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide molecular insights into the antiviral mechanism of IPB29 and suggest that incorporating the EAAAK sequence could enhance the efficacy of peptide-based therapeutics against SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is based on in vitro experiments, which may not fully represent in vivo conditions. However, the results are supported by direct comparisons and mechanistic analysis, providing moderate confidence in the conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the antiviral mechanism of IPB29, a potent SARS-CoV-2 fusion-inhibitory lipopeptide, and identifies the EAAAK sequence as a key factor in its enhanced activity. The findings suggest that this sequence could be a generalizable strategy for optimizing antiviral drug design. elements_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to elucidate the mechanism of action of IPB29, a potent SARS-CoV-2 fusion-inhibitory lipopeptide, and uncover insights into its enhanced antiviral activity. The background highlights the urgent need for effective therapeutics against SARS-CoV-2.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study characterized the mechanism of action of IPB29 and compared its antiviral activity with other lipopeptides, including IPB24 and IPB28, in different cell lines such as Huh-7, 293T/ACE2, and Vero E6-TMPRSS2 cells.
elements_en.methods: The researchers generated unconjugated template peptides, P43 (with EAAAK) and P37 (without EAAAK), and evaluated their inhibitory activity in various cell lines. They also used FITC-labeled lipopeptides for visualization of cellular uptake and compared the α-helicity and target-binding affinities of the peptides.
elements_en.main_results: IPB29 remained the most potent inhibitor of emerging Omicron subvariants compared to IPB24 and IPB28. P43 exhibited superior inhibitory activity compared to P37 in Huh-7 and 293T/ACE2 cells but not in Vero E6-TMPRSS2 cells. Both peptides showed comparable efficacy in blocking S protein-driven cell-cell fusion.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reveal that the EAAAK sequence in IPB29 is critical for its antiviral activity and functions via the endosomal fusion pathway, offering a generalizable strategy for optimizing antiviral drug design.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide molecular insights into the antiviral mechanism of IPB29 and suggest that incorporating the EAAAK sequence could enhance the efficacy of peptide-based therapeutics against SARS-CoV-2.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is based on in vitro experiments, which may not fully represent in vivo conditions. However, the results are supported by direct comparisons and mechanistic analysis, providing moderate confidence in the conclusions.

title_zh: 促进α-螺旋的氨基酸序列EAAAK显著增加严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2融合抑制肽通过内体融合途径的抗病毒药物活性。
source_body_en: UNLABELLED: The SARS-CoV-2 fusion-inhibitory lipopeptide IPB29 features a unique design incorporating the α-helix-promoting EAAAK sequence as a rigid linker between the peptide backbone and the conjugated lipid, exhibiting greatly improved antiviral activity compared to lipopeptides with conventional flexible linkers. Here, we characterized its mechanism of action and uncovered several critical insights. First, IPB29 remained the most potent inhibitor of emerging Omicron subvariants compared to IPB24 and IPB28, which share the same peptide sequence but employ flexible polyethylene glycol or glycine-serine repeat linker. Notably, this enhanced potency was abolished in Vero E6 cells stably expressing TMPRSS2, where viral entry occurs via the plasma membrane fusion pathway. Visualization using FITC-labeled lipopeptides demonstrated that IPB29 binds to and enters target cells more efficiently. Subsequently, we generated two unconjugated template peptides, P43 (containing EAAAK) and P37 (lacking EAAAK). P43 exhibited superior inhibitory activity compared to P37 in Huh-7 and 293T/ACE2 cells, but not in Vero E6-TMPRSS2 cells. Both peptides showed comparable efficacy in blocking S protein-driven cell-cell fusion. Although P43 displayed enhanced α-helicity relative to P37, both peptides exhibited similar target-binding affinities. Instead, the cellular uptake of P43 was markedly more efficient, further supporting that the improved antiviral effect is attributable to the inhibition of the viral endosomal fusion pathway. Collectively, our studies provide molecular insights into the antiviral mechanism of IPB29 and propose the short EAAAK sequence as a generalizable strategy for enhancing the efficacy of peptide-based therapeutics. IMPORTANCE: The development of effective therapeutics against SARS-CoV-2 remains an urgent priority. IPB29, a potent broad-spectrum lipopeptide fusion inhibitor currently in clinical trials, requires mechanistic elucidation. Here, we demonstrate that the C-terminal EAAAK motif in IPB29-originally designed as a rigid linker connecting the peptide backbone to the lipid moiety-is critical for its antiviral activity and functions via the endosomal fusion pathway. These findings reveal a generalizable strategy for optimizing antiviral drug design.
abstract_zh: UNLABELLED: 抗病毒药物IPB29融合抑制性脂肽具有独特的设计,其中α-螺旋促进的EAAAK序列作为肽骨架和连接脂质之间的刚性连接子,表现出比使用传统柔性连接子的脂肽大大增强的抗病毒活性。在此,我们对其作用机制进行了表征,并揭示了几项关键见解。首先,与IPB24和IPB28相比,IPB29对新兴的Omicron亚变体的抑制作用最强,IPB24和IPB28具有相同的肽序列,但使用的是聚乙二醇或甘氨酸-苏氨酸重复连接子。值得注意的是,这种增强的活性在稳定表达TMPRSS2的Vero E6细胞中被消除,因为病毒进入通过质膜融合途径发生。使用FITC标记的脂肽进行可视化显示,IPB29更有效地与靶细胞结合并进入靶细胞。随后,我们生成了两个未连接的模板肽,P43(包含EAAAK)和P37(缺乏EAAAK)。在Huh-7和293T/ACE2细胞中,P43的抑制活性优于P37,但在Vero E6-TMPRSS2细胞中则不然。两种肽在阻断S蛋白驱动的细胞-细胞融合方面表现出相似的效力。尽管P43相对于P37显示出增强的α-螺旋性,但两种肽在靶标结合亲和力方面表现出相似性。相反,P43在细胞摄取方面明显更有效,进一步支持了改进的抗病毒活性归因于抑制病毒内体融合途径。综上所述,我们的研究提供了关于IPB29抗病毒机制的分子见解,并提出了短EAAAK序列作为提高基于肽的治疗药物效力的通用策略。重要性:开发有效的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2抗病毒药物仍然是一个迫切的优先事项。IPB29是一种强效广谱脂肽融合抑制剂,目前正在临床试验中,需要阐明其作用机制。在此,我们证明了IPB29中的C-末端EAAAK基序(最初设计为连接肽骨架和脂质部分的刚性连接子)对于其抗病毒活性至关重要,并通过内体融合途径发挥作用。这些发现揭示了一种优化抗病毒药物药物设计的通用策略。

title: Longitudinal antibody correlates of SARS-CoV-2 infection in a US household cohort during Omicron waves
abstract: Background: SARS-CoV-2 vaccines have been updated based on circulating variants and the antibody protection from prior vaccination and infection against emerging variants. We evaluated longitudinal antibody correlates of SARS-CoV-2 infection risk during Omicron waves. Methods: We used data from a longitudinal cohort study from 2021 through 2025 with prospective surveillance for acute respiratory illness and repeated blood collection. A subset of participants also provided weekly respiratory specimens to identify asymptomatic infections. Serum samples were tested using multiplex assays measuring anti-Spike (S) binding IgG and angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) inhibition, a measure of inhibition of the ACE2 receptor interaction, across multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants. Cox models were used to evaluate associations between antibody levels, prior vaccination and infection, and SARS-CoV-2 infections. Findings: Among 119 participants who contributed 438.8 person-years of follow-up, 81 symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infections and 4 asymptomatic infections (from 33 participants with weekly swabs) were detected. Each two-fold increase in anti-S IgG concentration was associated with a 15% lower hazard of symptomatic infection (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.85, 95% CI: 0.82-0.88). Similarly, each 10% increase in ACE2 inhibition was associated with a 7% lower infection hazard (HR = 0.93, 95% CI: 0.90-0.95). After adjusting for antibody levels, prior SARS-CoV-2 infection remained protective, while recent vaccination was not associated with infection hazard. The peak predicted antibody level after repeated COVID-19 vaccinations was estimated to confer 62-65% protection against symptomatic infection. Interpretation: Higher levels of binding and functional antibodies were associated with reduced risk of SARS-CoV-2 infections across multiple waves between 2021-2025. These findings support the use of longitudinal serologic surveillance to inform vaccine evaluation and future booster strategies against evolving SARS-CoV-2 variants.

title: Sars Cov-2 Variants – Meta – Analysis
abstract: Background of the Study: SARS-COV-2 refers to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2. It belongs to family Coronaviridae, subfamily Coronavirinae and β genera. Coronaviruses are crown-shaped particles with spikes protruding from their surface. The SARS-CoV-2 genome is a 29.9 kb positive-sense single-stranded RNA molecule containing 14 ORFs encoding four structural and 16 non-structural ones. Proteins (nsp 1-16). Structural proteins include spike protein (S), envelope protein (E), membrane protein (M) and nucleoprotein (N). Non-structural proteins are involved in viral RNA replication and gene expression, forming an RNA synthesis complex in which nsp12 functions as an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase. Unlike other RNA viruses, coronaviruses have RNA proofreading machinery to correct genetic mutations due to nsp14 3′-5′ exonuclease activity. However, it has been estimated that SARS-CoV-2 undergoes 3 × 10–6 mutations per nucleotide per replication cycle Aims & Objective: The aim of this study is to review the spread of current variants of SARS-CoV-viruses. To look at the disease profile of different variants of SARS CoV-2 Virus. To look at the current variants of SARS CoV-2 Virus prevalent in different parts of the world. Methods: A Meta analysis method is used to study about corona virus and its variants. Data was collected from various publications in indexed journals, recent editions of textbooks, website of CDC, NCDC, WHO. Follow by Prisma, at first stage of the search, 280 articles were found, and after reviewing the titles of the articles, 120 duplicate and overlapping articles were deleted and 160 articles remained. In total, 60 articles were removed due to noncompliance with the criteria, the extract of 40 potentially related articles were reviewed, and 50 articles were excluded due to lack of access to the full text articles. Finally, 10 appropriate papers were selected to enter the meta-analysis stage. Results: SARS-CoV-2 spike mutations can increase transmissibility and immune escape, while some recurrent mutations may reduce disease severity. It also finds limited cross-protection across related coronaviruses, evidence of recombination in SARS-CoV, and stronger ACE2 binding that may help explain faster spread. SARS-CoV was detected in 329 of 436 patients, or 75%, and human metapneumovirus in 41 of 335 patients, or 12%; other respiratory pathogens were rare. The macaque experiment further showed all 4 infected macaques shed virus, and 3 of 4 developed lung damage similar to human SARS. Conclusion: COVID-19, a novel coronavirus first detected in Wuhan in December 2019, caused a global pandemic and prompted widespread public-health measures and vaccine development. The outbreak reduced active cases through vaccination but exposed major gaps in pandemic preparedness, prompting calls for stronger long-term readiness.

title: COVID-19 and pregnancy: is a "forgotten" disease still a threat?
abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), has significantly affected global health, including maternal and perinatal outcomes. Although the acute phase of the pandemic has subsided, the continued emergence of new viral variants, waning population immunity, and suboptimal vaccination coverage among women of reproductive age suggest that COVID-19 in pregnancy may remain a clinically relevant problem. This review summarizes current evidence regarding the clinical course, complications, and prevention of SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy, addressing whether COVID-19 should be considered a "forgotten" obstetric disease. Most pregnant women develop asymptomatic or mild infection; however, pregnancy is associated with an increased risk of severe disease, intensive care unit admission, mechanical ventilation, and maternal mortality, particularly among women of advanced maternal age, with obesity, comorbidities, or without vaccination. SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy is consistently linked with a higher incidence of preeclampsia, including severe forms such as eclampsia and HELLP syndrome, increased rates of cesarean delivery and, in many populations, preterm birth. Vertical transmission is uncommon but documented. Severe placental involvement, referred to as COVID-19 placentitis, may result in placental insufficiency, fetal hypoxia, and stillbirth. Expression of angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 within the placenta provides a biological basis for viral tropism and potential disruption of placental defense mechanisms, contributing to adverse perinatal outcomes. COVID-19 vaccination before conception, during pregnancy, and throughout breastfeeding is safe and effective. Immunization significantly reduces the risk of severe maternal disease, preterm birth, emergency cesarean delivery, stillbirth, and neonatal hospitalization, while also conferring passive protection to infants. Maintaining up-to-date vaccination remains essential for preventing maternal and perinatal complications associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the impact of SARS-CoV-2 on pregnancy, focusing on clinical outcomes, complications, and prevention strategies. It highlights that while most pregnant women experience asymptomatic or mild infections, the risk of severe disease, ICU admission, mechanical ventilation, and maternal mortality is heightened, especially in those with advanced maternal age, obesity, or comorbidities. The review also notes that SARS-CoV-2 infection is associated with increased rates of preeclampsia, cesarean delivery, and preterm birth. Despite the pandemic's decline, new variants and suboptimal vaccination rates among reproductive-age women suggest ongoing clinical relevance. The findings emphasize the importance of vaccination during pregnancy and breastfeeding for maternal and perinatal protection.

title: Increased receptor binding and spike glycosylation, remodeled immune escape of surging SARS-CoV-2 subvariant BA.3.2.2/RE.2.2/Cicada.
abstract: SARS-CoV-2 continues to evolve. The subvariant BA.3.2 (Cicada), a derivative of the Omicron BA.3 subtype first detected in late 2024, harbors multiple spike protein mutations, ORF7 and ORF8 deletions, and has recently evolved sublineages (BA.3.2.1 and BA.3.2.2), rendering it a critical target for epidemiological surveillance. The BA.3.2.2 sublineage, represented by RE.2.2, shows a marked upward trend in late 2025. Using surface plasmon resonance, we found that RE.2.2's spike (S) protein receptor-binding domain (RBD) exhibits relatively high affinity for human receptor angiotensin-converting enzyme 2, with structural analysis identifying the R493Q reverse mutation as the key determinant. Pseudovirus infection and antibody neutralization assays demonstrated that RE.2.2 exhibited a distinct neutralization profile compared to contemporaneous dominant subvariants. Notably, several antibodies that previously lacked neutralizing activity (e.g., S2K146 and L4.65) to other subvariants regained neutralizing potency against RE.2.2, which was associated with key mutations including G446D. Profiling of RE.2.2 RBD binding to ACE2 orthologs across species showed no significant difference in species tropism from the representative Omicron BA.1. Importantly, RE.2.2 exhibits the newly emerged N-linked glycosylation at spike protein N529 (absent in all other subvariants), a modification potentially associated with immune evasion or spike protein conformational dynamics. In addition, we corroborated the "O-follow-N" glycosylation observation as previously reported, where O-linked glycans preferentially localize near N-glycosylation sites, implying coordinated glycan organization as an extra layer of spike regulation. These findings illuminate the evolutionary characteristics, functional changes, and the constrained virus immune escape of BA.3.2.2 (RE.2.2), providing critical insights into antibody development and variant surveillance.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focused on the BA.3.2.2 sublineage, represented by RE.2.2, which shows a marked upward trend in late 2025. The research involved surface plasmon resonance, pseudovirus infection, and antibody neutralization assays.
analysis.methods: The BA.3.2.2 sublineage was analyzed using surface plasmon resonance to assess receptor-binding domain (RBD) affinity for human angiotensin-converting enzyme 2. Pseudovirus infection and antibody neutralization assays were conducted to evaluate neutralization profiles and antibody activity.
analysis.main_results: RE.2.2's spike (S) protein RBD exhibits high affinity for human ACE2. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings have implications for antibody development and variant surveillance, enhancing our understanding of the virus's immune escape mechanisms and potential for future variants.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the absence of direct clinical outcomes and the need for further validation of the observed effects. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational nature of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed the BA.3.2.2 sublineage of SARS-CoV-2, showing high affinity for human ACE2 and novel glycosylation. Key mutations, such as G446D, enable immune evasion, providing insights for antibody development and variant surveillance.

title_zh: 受体结合增加和刺突糖基化,重塑免疫逃逸的迅速蔓延的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 亚变异株 BA.3.2.2/RE.2.2/Cicada。
source_body_en: SARS-CoV-2 continues to evolve. The subvariant BA.3.2 (Cicada), a derivative of the Omicron BA.3 subtype first detected in late 2024, harbors multiple spike protein mutations, ORF7 and ORF8 deletions, and has recently evolved sublineages (BA.3.2.1 and BA.3.2.2), rendering it a critical target for epidemiological surveillance. The BA.3.2.2 sublineage, represented by RE.2.2, shows a marked upward trend in late 2025. Using surface plasmon resonance, we found that RE.2.2's spike (S) protein receptor-binding domain (RBD) exhibits relatively high affinity for human receptor angiotensin-converting enzyme 2, with structural analysis identifying the R493Q reverse mutation as the key determinant. Pseudovirus infection and antibody neutralization assays demonstrated that RE.2.2 exhibited a distinct neutralization profile compared to contemporaneous dominant subvariants. Notably, several antibodies that previously lacked neutralizing activity (e.g., S2K146 and L4.65) to other subvariants regained neutralizing potency against RE.2.2, which was associated with key mutations including G446D. Profiling of RE.2.2 RBD binding to ACE2 orthologs across species showed no significant difference in species tropism from the representative Omicron BA.1. Importantly, RE.2.2 exhibits the newly emerged N-linked glycosylation at spike protein N529 (absent in all other subvariants), a modification potentially associated with immune evasion or spike protein conformational dynamics. In addition, we corroborated the "O-follow-N" glycosylation observation as previously reported, where O-linked glycans preferentially localize near N-glycosylation sites, implying coordinated glycan organization as an extra layer of spike regulation. These findings illuminate the evolutionary characteristics, functional changes, and the constrained virus immune escape of BA.3.2.2 (RE.2.2), providing critical insights into antibody development and variant surveillance.
abstract_zh: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 仍在不断进化。子变体 BA.3.2(蝉),源自 2024 年末首次发现的 Omicron BA.3 子型,携带多个 刺突蛋白 突变、ORF7 和 ORF8 缺失,并且最近进化出亚分支(BA.3.2.1 和 BA.3.2.2),使其成为流行病学监测的关键目标。BA.3.2.2 亚分支,由 RE.2.2 代表,在 2025 年末表现出明显的上升趋势。通过表面等离子共振技术,我们发现 RE.2.2 的刺突(S)蛋白受体结合域(RBD)对人类受体血管紧张素转换酶 2(ACE2)具有相对较高的亲和力,结构分析表明 R493Q 逆突变 是关键决定因素。假病毒感染和抗体中和试验表明,RE.2.2 在中和谱型上与同期主导亚变体表现出显著差异。值得注意的是,一些之前缺乏中和活性的抗体(如 S2K146 和 L4.65)对其他亚变体重新获得了中和活性,这与关键突变 包括 G446D 相关。对 RE.2.2 RBD 与 ACE2 同源物在不同物种间的结合进行谱型分析显示,其物种嗜性与代表性的 Omicron BA.1 无显著差异。重要的是,RE.2.2 表现出在 刺突蛋白 N529(其他所有亚变体均不存在)处新出现的 N-连接糖基化,这一修饰可能与免疫逃逸或刺突蛋白 构象动力学相关。此外,我们证实了先前报道的“O-随-N”糖基化现象,其中 O-连接糖基化优先定位在 N-糖基化位点附近,暗示协调的糖基化组织作为刺突调控的额外层。这些发现揭示了 BA.3.2.2(RE.2.2)的进化特征、功能变化及其受限制的病毒免疫逃逸,为抗体开发和变异监测提供了关键见解。
summary_zh: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 仍在不断进化。子变体 BA.3.2(蝉),源自 2024 年末首次发现的 Omicron BA.3 子型,携带多个 刺突蛋白 突变、ORF7 和 ORF8 缺失,并且最近进化出亚分支(BA.3.2.1 和 BA.3.2.2),使其成为流行病学监测的关键目标。BA.3.2.2 亚分支,由 RE.2.2 代表,在 2025 年末表现出明显的上升趋势。通过表面等离子共振技术,我们发现 RE.2.2 的刺突(S)蛋白受体结合域(RBD)对人类受体血管紧张素转换酶 2(ACE2)具有相对较高的亲和力,结构分析表明 R493Q 逆突变 是关键决定因素。假病毒感染和抗体中和试验表明,RE.2.2 在中和谱型上与同期主导亚变体表现出显著差异。值得注意的是,一些之前缺乏中和活性的抗体(如 S2K146 和 L4.65)对其他亚变体重新获得了中和活性,这与关键突变 包括 G446D 相关。对 RE.2.2 RBD 与 ACE2 同源物在不同物种间的结合进行谱型分析显示,其物种嗜性与代表性的 Omicron BA.1 无显著差异。重要的是,RE.2.2 表现出在 刺突蛋白 N529(其他所有亚变体均不存在)处新出现的 N-连接糖基化,这一修饰可能与免疫逃逸或刺突蛋白 构象动力学相关。此外,我们证实了先前报道的“O-随-N”糖基化现象,其中 O-连接糖基化优先定位在 N-糖基化位点附近,暗示协调的糖基化组织作为刺突调控的额外层。这些发现揭示了 BA.3.2.2(RE.2.2)的进化特征、功能变化及其受限制的病毒免疫逃逸,为抗体开发和变异监测提供了关键见解。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 继续进化。亚变种 BA.3.2 (Cicada) 是奥密克戎 BA.3 亚型的衍生物,近期演化出亚分支 (BA.3.2.1 和 BA.3.2.2),使其成为流行病学的关键目标 监测。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究聚焦于BA.3.2.2亚系,以RE.2.2为代表,显示出2025年末显著上升的趋势。研究涉及表面等离子体共振、假病毒感染和抗体中和试验。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用表面等离子体共振技术对BA.3.2.2亚系进行了分析,以评估其受体结合域(RBD)对人类血管紧张素转换酶2的亲和力。进行了伪病毒感染和抗体中和试验,以评估中和谱型和抗体活性。
analysis_zh.main_results: RE.2.2的刺突蛋白(S)受体结合域(RBD)对人类ACE2表现出高亲和力。值得注意的是,一些先前无法中和的抗体重新获得了对RE.2.2的中和能力,这与关键的突变突变G446D相关。RE.2.2还在刺突蛋白位点出现了一个新出现的N连接糖基化位点N529。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现阐明了BA.3.2.2 (RE.2.2)的进化特征、功能变化和免疫逃逸机制,为抗体开发和变异株监测提供了关键见解。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现对抗体开发和变异株 监测 有重要意义,有助于我们更好地理解病毒的免疫逃逸机制及未来变异株的潜在可能性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括缺乏直接临床结果以及需要进一步验证所观察到的效果。由于研究的观察性质,证据强度为中等。

title: Head Lice: A Revised View of the Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Transmission and Prevalence.
abstract: Background Head louse transmission is a regular occurrence among children when coming into close contact with others during social activities. During the Covid-19 pandemic most countries instituted lockdown periods resulting in isolation of children away from regular contacts, potentially restricting opportunities for louse transmission. Subsequently there were reports of reduced infestations in children at schools, compared with before the pandemic, with a parallel fall in sales of pediculicidal treatments in several countries beyond the longer-term decline in product sales observed over several years before the pandemic. Methods For this narrative review all literature linking Covid-19 and head lice were revisited and re-evaluated. Results Despite the increased opportunity for elimination of infestations, some households with no outside contacts reported persistent incidence of head louse infestation and a review of the various studies suggests that most reported changes in head louse prevalence were relatively short lived or even illusory and in countries with low or middle incomes there was little or no difference in prevalence as a result of lockdowns. Conclusions Some aspects of the social distancing imposed in several countries during the pandemic appear to have continued to have some effect on social interactions of children, particularly in Western countries, with a commensurate slower recovery of head louse prevalence in some communities.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on head louse transmission and prevalence among children, focusing on the social interactions and contact patterns affected by lockdowns.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review revisited and re-evaluated all literature linking the COVID-19 pandemic to head lice, using a narrative approach without explicit meta-analysis or pooled estimates.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: There was a reported reduction in head louse infestations and sales of pediculicidal treatments in several countries during the pandemic, but these changes were often short-lived or illusory, with little impact in low and middle-income countries.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights the heterogeneity in reported changes in head louse prevalence, with some households reporting persistent infestations despite lockdowns, and suggests that the social distancing measures had a limited and variable effect on head louse transmission.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to understand the long-term effects of social distancing on head louse prevalence, and to develop more effective strategies for managing head lice in the context of ongoing social changes.

analysis.summary_en: This review found that while there were initial reports of reduced head louse infestations during the COVID-19 pandemic, these changes were often short-lived and varied across different regions, with little impact in low and middle-income countries. Further research is needed to understand the long-term effects of social distancing on head louse prevalence.

title: The COVID-19 Trajectory in Israel: A Comprehensive Analysis of National Surveillance Data on Documented Infections, Test Positivity, and Vaccine-Effectiveness Estimates
abstract: Abstract Background Israel was among the first countries to implement rapid nationwide BNT162b2 vaccination and became a major source of early real-world evidence on COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness. Early Israeli studies reported approximately 90–95% effectiveness against documented SARS-CoV-2 infection, but over relatively short epidemiological periods. This study examines the national trajectory from the pre-vaccination period through the end of the global COVID-19 emergency. Methods Five publicly available Israeli Ministry of Health surveillance datasets were analyzed longitudinally from February 2020 through May 2023. National trajectories of documented infection and test positivity were characterized before and after vaccine rollout, which began on December 20, 2020. Vaccinated–unvaccinated differences were then examined in two ways: first, using routine-surveillance case rates by vaccination status; and second, using an age-adjusted test-positivity analysis among individuals without documented prior infection, with testing denominators stratified by vaccination status. The second analysis, designed to address potential biases from prior-infection history and differential testing, began 19 weeks later, when the required data became available on May 30, 2021. Results The two completed pre-rollout waves declined to ≤10% of their peaks within 32 and 43 days, respectively. The winter 2020–2021 wave, which was already underway when vaccination began, required 68 days. Subsequent major peaks were larger than the January 2021 peak, with Delta 17% higher and Omicron approximately nine times higher. Routine surveillance reached an early apparent vaccine-effectiveness peak of 94.4% in mid-February 2021 and declined to 61.5% by late May, with substantial rebounds thereafter. By early December it was 79.9%, before falling to 37.4% two weeks later and 8.2% by late December; it became persistently negative in February 2022. The test-positivity analysis showed a generally lower trajectory. After unstable estimates during the low-incidence summer weeks, it reached 62.1% in early December, fell to 26.8% one week later and -14.5% the next, and remained negative thereafter. Conclusions These observational data cannot establish causal vaccine effects and do not address protection against hospitalization, severe disease, or death. Within the domain of documented infection, however, the early vaccination-associated advantage attenuated substantially within months and was further reduced when prior-infection history and vaccination-stratified testing were incorporated; in the latter analysis, the contrast reversed by late 2021 and remained negative thereafter. At the population level, national surveillance showed no sustained reduction in the magnitude or resolution of documented-infection waves after rollout. The Israeli experience may therefore be informative for future public-health emergencies, in which early short-window effectiveness estimates may change substantially as population immunity, testing practices, and the pathogen itself evolve.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to analyze the national trajectory of documented infections and vaccine effectiveness of SARS-CoV-2 in Israel, leveraging early real-world evidence from rapid nationwide vaccination.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed five publicly available Israeli Ministry of Health surveillance datasets from February 2020 through May 2023, focusing on documented infections, test positivity, and vaccine effectiveness across the population.
analysis_en.methods: Vaccinated–unvaccinated differences were examined using routine-surveillance case rates and an age-adjusted test-positivity analysis among individuals without documented prior infection, with testing denominators stratified by vaccination status.
analysis_en.main_results: Routine surveillance showed an early apparent vaccine-effectiveness peak of 94.4% in mid-February 2021, which declined to 61.5% by late May and rebounded thereafter. The test-positivity analysis showed a generally lower trajectory, with estimates reaching 62.1% in early December, falling to 26.8% one week later and -14.5% the next, and remaining negative thereafter.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights that early vaccine effectiveness estimates against documented infection may change substantially over time due to evolving population immunity, testing practices, and the pathogen itself.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform future public-health emergencies by demonstrating how early vaccine effectiveness estimates can shift as immunity, testing behaviors, and viral variants evolve.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The observational data cannot establish causal vaccine effects and do not address protection against hospitalization, severe disease, or death, limiting the strength of the conclusions to moderate.

title_zh: The COVID-19 Trajectory in Israel: A Comprehensive Analysis of National Surveillance Data on Documented Infections, Test Positivity, and Vaccine-Effectiveness Estimates
source_body_en: Abstract Background Israel was among the first countries to implement rapid nationwide BNT162b2 vaccination and became a major source of early real-world evidence on COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness. Early Israeli studies reported approximately 90–95% effectiveness against documented SARS-CoV-2 infection, but over relatively short epidemiological periods. This study examines the national trajectory from the pre-vaccination period through the end of the global COVID-19 emergency. Methods Five publicly available Israeli Ministry of Health surveillance datasets were analyzed longitudinally from February 2020 through May 2023. National trajectories of documented infection and test positivity were characterized before and after vaccine rollout, which began on December 20, 2020. Vaccinated–unvaccinated differences were then examined in two ways: first, using routine-surveillance case rates by vaccination status; and second, using an age-adjusted test-positivity analysis among individuals without documented prior infection, with testing denominators stratified by vaccination status. The second analysis, designed to address potential biases from prior-infection history and differential testing, began 19 weeks later, when the required data became available on May 30, 2021. Results The two completed pre-rollout waves declined to ≤10% of their peaks within 32 and 43 days, respectively. The winter 2020–2021 wave, which was already underway when vaccination began, required 68 days. Subsequent major peaks were larger than the January 2021 peak, with Delta 17% higher and Omicron approximately nine times higher. Routine surveillance reached an early apparent vaccine-effectiveness peak of 94.4% in mid-February 2021 and declined to 61.5% by late May, with substantial rebounds thereafter. By early December it was 79.9%, before falling to 37.4% two weeks later and 8.2% by late December; it became persistently negative in February 2022. The test-positivity analysis showed a generally lower trajectory. After unstable estimates during the low-incidence summer weeks, it reached 62.1% in early December, fell to 26.8% one week later and -14.5% the next, and remained negative thereafter. Conclusions These observational data cannot establish causal vaccine effects and do not address protection against hospitalization, severe disease, or death. Within the domain of documented infection, however, the early vaccination-associated advantage attenuated substantially within months and was further reduced when prior-infection history and vaccination-stratified testing were incorporated; in the latter analysis, the contrast reversed by late 2021 and remained negative thereafter. At the population level, national surveillance showed no sustained reduction in the magnitude or resolution of documented-infection waves after rollout. The Israeli experience may therefore be informative for future public-health emergencies, in which early short-window effectiveness estimates may change substantially as population immunity, testing practices, and the pathogen itself evolve.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 以色列是首批实施全国快速接种BNT162b2 疫苗接种的国家之一,并成为早期真实世界证据的主要来源,用于评估新型冠状病毒感染 疫苗的效果。早期的以色列研究报告称,针对记录的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染,疫苗有效性约为90–95%,但仅限于相对较短的流行病学时期。本研究考察了从疫苗接种接种前时期到全球新型冠状病毒感染紧急状态结束的国家轨迹。方法 分析了五个自2020年2月至2023年5月公开的以色列卫生部监测数据集。在疫苗接种开始于2020年12月20日之前和之后,分别描述了记录感染和检测阳性率的国家轨迹。随后,通过两种方式分析了接种疫苗与未接种疫苗之间的差异:首先,使用常规监测的病例率,按疫苗接种状态进行分类;其次,对无记录既往感染的个体进行年龄调整的检测阳性率分析,其中检测分母按疫苗接种状态分层。第二种分析旨在解决既往感染史和检测差异可能带来的偏倚问题,该分析从2021年5月30日开始,即所需数据可用后19周。结果 两个已完成的接种前波峰分别在32天和43天内降至其峰值的≤10%。2020–2021年冬季的波峰,其接种开始时已经发生,需要68天才能下降。随后的主要波峰比2021年1月的波峰更大,Delta变异株感染率高出17%,而Omicron变异株感染率则大约高出九倍。常规监测在2021年2月中旬显示出早期明显的疫苗效果峰值为94.4%,到2021年5月下旬下降至61.5%,之后出现显著反弹。到2021年12月初,该比例回升至79.9%,随后在两周后降至37.4%,到2021年底12月降至8.2%;2022年2月后,该比例持续为负。检测阳性率分析显示总体趋势较低。在低发病率的夏季几周内,估计值不稳定,到2021年12月初达到62.1%,一周后降至26.8%,接着降至-14.5%,之后一直保持负值。结论 这些观察性数据无法确立疫苗的效果因果关系,也未涉及对住院、重症或死亡的保护作用。然而,在记录感染的领域内,早期与疫苗接种相关的优势在几个月内显著减弱,并且在纳入既往感染史和按疫苗接种状态分层的检测后进一步降低;在后者分析中,到2021年底对比结果逆转并持续为负。在人口层面,全国监测接种后,记录感染波峰的强度和消退程度未出现持续下降。因此,以色列的经验可能对未来公共卫生紧急事件具有参考价值,其中早期短期窗口期的疫苗效果估计可能会随着群体免疫力、检测实践和病原体本身的演变而发生显著变化。

title: Using large language models to facilitate literature review and data extraction for infectious disease models: COVID-19 as a test case
abstract: Infectious disease transmission models are governed by parameters informed by systematic review of epidemiological literature. Large language models (LLMs) could facilitate this, but the reliability of the results to inform models has not been tested. We built an open-source, end-to-end pipeline to simulate LLM performance in a hypothetical scenario where they were available to inform COVID-19 models developed during the first four months of 2020. It screened articles and extracted the reproduction number, serial interval, and incubation period from full-text PDFs. We applied it to 2,067 PubMed/medRxiv records published 31 December 2019–30 April 2020 using four models (GPT-5-mini, GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.8 and Gemini 2.5 Pro) and evaluated it against full-corpus human screening and 50-article extraction gold standards. We combined models post hoc, pooled the extracted values into an infectious disease (SEIR) model, and ran sensitivity analyses to test approaches to improve extraction accuracy. Screening sensitivity was 0.72-0.95 and specificity 0.92-0.99. For articles reporting few values, extraction F1 was 0.90-0.96 with precision 0.91-1.00; across all articles, including those with dozens of stratified estimates, recall fell to 0.38-0.78. No fabricated values observed; errors were misassignments of values filed under the wrong parameter, or borrowed values treated as the study’s own. Incomplete extraction from dense articles was mainly due to prompting and output format, not model capability. Ensembling allowed recall-precision trade-offs, and correctness increased with model agreement, from about 30% at one vote to 92-95% at four. The pipeline processed the corpus in hours versus an estimated 130-265 person-hours of manual effort. Our results show that current models can extract transmission parameters from unstructured literature accurately enough to inform outbreak modelling. The bottleneck lies in task specification, and careful prompt and output schema design are key to reducing misassignment errors. Human effort is best directed at workflow development and provenance validation.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the use of large language models (LLMs) to extract epidemiological parameters from literature to inform infectious disease models, using SARS-CoV-2 as a test case. The study developed an open-source pipeline to simulate LLM performance in a hypothetical scenario where they were used to inform models during the early stages of the pandemic. The pipeline extracted key parameters such as reproduction number, serial interval, and incubation period from 2,067 articles published between December 2019 and April 2020. The results showed that LLMs could extract transmission parameters with sufficient accuracy to inform outbreak modeling, though challenges remained in task specification and reducing misassignment errors. The authors emphasize the importance of careful prompt and output schema design, as well as human validation in workflow development. The study highlights the potential of LLMs in accelerating literature review and data extraction processes for infectious disease modeling.

title: Outcomes of immunocompromised and non-immunocompromised patients in the ICU diverge late in the pandemic.
abstract: RATIONALE: The impact of immunocompromising conditions on outcomes in critically ill patients with COVID-19 remains poorly characterized. We hypothesized that disparities in COVID-19 outcomes in immunocompromised patients may differ by viral strain and time course of the pandemic. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR positive patients admitted to intensive care (ICU) at Stanford from March 2020 to July 2022 using electronic medical records. Immunocompromised status included solid organ transplant; hematologic malignancy/transplant; solid cancer with metastases and recent chemotherapy; HIV/AIDS; and connective tissue disease on immunosuppression. SARS-CoV-2 strain periods were classified as pre-Delta (3/2020-8/2021), Delta (9/2021-12/2021), and Omicron (1/2022-7/2022). We assessed 90-day survival differences between immunocompromised and non-immunocompromised patients by strain using Cox-proportional hazards, adjusted for age, sex, and APACHE II score. RESULTS: A total of 791 patients were included, 450 from the pre-Delta period, 114 from the Delta period, and 227 from the Omicron period. We compared 633 non-immunocompromised patients with 158 immunocompromised patients (77 during the pre-Delta, 22 Delta, and 59 Omicron periods). Patients admitted during the Omicron period were more likely to be immunocompromised (26%) compared to pre-Delta (17%) or Delta periods (19%; p = 0.008). Immunocompromise was associated with worse outcomes in the entire cohort after adjustment (HR 1.68, 95% CI 1.2-2.3, p < 0.001). However, when stratified by strain period, immunocompromised status was only significantly associated with higher 90-day mortality in patients from the Omicron period (42% vs 17%, HR 2.9, CI% 1.7-5.0, p < 0.001). Differences in mortality between immunocompromised and immunocompetent patients were not statistically different in either the pre-Delta (34% vs. 23%, HR 1.4, 95% CI 0.9-2.1, p = 0.15) or Delta periods (32% vs. 28% HR 1.0, 95% CI 0.4-2.5, p = 0.92). Notably, survival was significantly improved during the Omicron period compared to earlier strain periods in immunocompetent patients (HR 0.6, 95% CI 0.4-0.9, p = 0.02) but not for immunocompromised patients (HR 1.4, 95% CI 0.80-2.44, p = 0.24). CONCLUSION: In this retrospective cohort analysis of patients admitted to the ICU due to SARS-CoV-2 infection, we found that lower survival among immunocompromised patients was due to higher mortality during the Omicron period, with similar mortality between immunocompetent and immunocompromised patients during other periods.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study investigates the outcomes of immunocompromised and non-immunocompromised patients in the ICU during different periods of the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, focusing on how these outcomes diverge over time. The central question is whether immunocompromised status affects mortality rates differently across viral strain periods, particularly pre-Delta, Delta, and Omicron.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a retrospective cohort analysis of SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR positive patients admitted to the ICU at Stanford from March 2020 to July 2022. The study used electronic medical records and classified SARS-CoV-2 strain periods as pre-Delta (March 2020-August 2021), Delta (September 2021-December 2021), and Omicron (January 2022-July 2022). Immunocompromised status was defined based on conditions such as solid organ transplant, hematologic malignancy/transplant, solid cancer with metastases and recent chemotherapy, HIV/AIDS, and connective tissue disease on immunosuppression. The analysis employed Cox-proportional hazards to assess 90-day survival differences, adjusting for age, sex, and APACHE II score.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study found that immunocompromised patients had worse outcomes overall, with a hazard ratio of 1.68 (95% CI 1.2-2.3, p < 0.001). However, when stratified by strain period, immunocompromised status was only significantly associated with higher 90-day mortality in the Omicron period (42% vs 17%, HR 2.9, CI 1.7-5.0, p < 0.001). In contrast, during the pre-Delta and Delta periods, there was no significant difference in mortality between immunocompromised and non-immunocompromised patients. Notably, survival improved for immunocompetent patients during the Omicron period compared to earlier periods, but this improvement was not observed for immunocompromised patients.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study acknowledges that the association between immunocompromised status and mortality was not consistent across all strain periods. Specifically, during the pre-Delta and Delta periods, the difference in mortality between immunocompromised and non-immunocompromised patients was not statistically significant. This suggests potential heterogeneity in outcomes based on viral strain and pandemic timeline. Additionally, the study does not provide information on the mechanisms underlying the observed differences in mortality or the specific factors contributing to improved survival in immunocompetent patients during the Omicron period.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings highlight the need for further research to understand the mechanisms behind the divergent outcomes of immunocompromised patients during different phases of the pandemic. It also underscores the importance of continued surveillance and tailored interventions for immunocompromised individuals, particularly during the Omicron period. Future studies should explore the impact of specific viral variants and the role of immunosuppressive therapies in influencing patient outcomes.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该研究探讨了在严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2大流行的不同阶段,免疫功能受损和免疫功能正常的ICU患者结局,重点关注这些结局随时间的变化情况。核心问题是免疫功能受损状态是否在不同病毒株时期(特别是Delta前、Delta和Omicron时期)对死亡率率产生不同的影响。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这项回顾性分析是针对2020年3月至2022年7月期间被收治在斯坦福大学重症监护病房(ICU)的队列研究 RT-PCR阳性患者的回顾性分析。研究使用电子病历,并将严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2毒株时期分为三个阶段:Delta前(2020年3月至2021年8月)、Delta(2021年9月至2021年12月)和Omicron(2022年1月至2022年7月)。免疫功能低下状态的定义基于诸如实体器官移植、血液系统恶性肿瘤/移植、伴有转移的实体癌及近期化疗、HIV/AIDS以及免疫抑制的结缔组织疾病等条件。分析采用Cox比例风险模型评估90天生存率差异,并调整年龄、性别和APACHE II评分。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该研究发现,免疫功能低下患者总体预后较差,其风险比为1.68(95% CI 1.2-2.3,p < 0.001)。然而,当按病毒株时期分层分析时,免疫功能低下状态仅在奥密克戎时期与更高的90天死亡率显著相关(42% vs 17%,HR 2.9,CI 1.7-5.0,p < 0.001)。相比之下,在Delta变异株出现前和Delta时期,免疫功能低下与非免疫功能低下患者之间的死亡率无显著差异。值得注意的是,与之前时期相比,免疫功能正常患者在奥密克戎时期生存率有所改善,但这种改善在免疫功能低下患者中并未观察到。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该研究承认,免疫功能低下状态与死亡率之间的关联并非在所有病毒株时期都一致。具体而言,在新冠Delta变异株之前和Delta变异株时期,免疫功能低下患者与非免疫功能低下患者在死亡率方面的差异并不具有统计学意义。这表明病毒株和疫情时间线可能导致结果的异质性。此外,该研究未提供关于观察到的死亡率差异的潜在机制,或在Omicron时期免疫功能正常患者生存率提高的具体因素的信息。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 这些发现强调了需要进一步研究以了解免疫功能低下患者在疫情不同阶段出现不同结果的机制。它还突显了持续进行监测以及为免疫功能低下人群制定针对性干预措施的重要性,尤其是在奥密克戎时期。未来的研究应探讨特定病毒变异株的影响以及免疫抑制治疗在影响患者结果中的作用。

CONCLUSION: In this retrospective cohort analysis of patients admitted to the ICU due to SARS-CoV-2 infection, we found that lower survival among immunocompromised patients was due to higher mortality during the Omicron period, with similar mortality between immunocompetent and immunocompromised patients during other periods.

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该研究探讨了在严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2大流行的不同阶段,免疫功能受损和免疫功能正常的ICU患者结局,重点关注这些结局随时间的变化情况。核心问题是免疫功能受损状态是否在不同病毒株时期(特别是Delta前、Delta和Omicron时期)对死亡率率产生不同的影响。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这项回顾性分析是针对2020年3月至2022年7月期间被收治在斯坦福大学重症监护病房(ICU)的队列研究 RT-PCR阳性患者的回顾性分析。研究使用电子病历,并将严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2毒株时期分为三个阶段:Delta前(2020年3月至2021年8月)、Delta(2021年9月至2021年12月)和Omicron(2022年1月至2022年7月)。免疫功能低下状态的定义基于诸如实体器官移植、血液系统恶性肿瘤/移植、伴有转移的实体癌及近期化疗、HIV/AIDS以及免疫抑制的结缔组织疾病等条件。分析采用Cox比例风险模型评估90天生存率差异,并调整年龄、性别和APACHE II评分。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该研究发现,免疫功能低下患者总体预后较差,其风险比为1.68(95% CI 1.2-2.3,p < 0.001)。然而,当按病毒株时期分层分析时,免疫功能低下状态仅在奥密克戎时期与更高的90天死亡率显著相关(42% vs 17%,HR 2.9,CI 1.7-5.0,p < 0.001)。相比之下,在Delta变异株出现前和Delta时期,免疫功能低下与非免疫功能低下患者之间的死亡率无显著差异。值得注意的是,与之前时期相比,免疫功能正常患者在奥密克戎时期生存率有所改善,但这种改善在免疫功能低下患者中并未观察到。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该研究承认,免疫功能低下状态与死亡率之间的关联并非在所有病毒株时期都一致。具体而言,在新冠Delta变异株之前和Delta变异株时期,免疫功能低下患者与非免疫功能低下患者在死亡率方面的差异并不具有统计学意义。这表明病毒株和疫情时间线可能导致结果的异质性。此外,该研究未提供关于观察到的死亡率差异的潜在机制,或在Omicron时期免疫功能正常患者生存率提高的具体因素的信息。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 这些发现强调了需要进一步研究以了解免疫功能低下患者在疫情不同阶段出现不同结果的机制。它还突显了持续进行监测以及为免疫功能低下人群制定针对性干预措施的重要性,尤其是在奥密克戎时期。未来的研究应探讨特定病毒变异株的影响以及免疫抑制治疗在影响患者结果中的作用。

title: Post-traumatic stress disorder following intensive care for COVID-19: a single-center retrospective follow-up study.
abstract: Severe COVID-19 frequently required prolonged intensive care, including mechanical ventilation or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Survivors of such critical illness may develop post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). We conducted a single-center retrospective follow-up study of COVID-19 ICU survivors at Saarland University Medical Center, Germany, assessing ICD-11 trauma-related disorders using the validated International Trauma Questionnaire (ITQ) and analyzing associations with clinical factors. Of 110 eligible patients, 42 (38.2%) valid datasets were obtained. The overall prevalence of ICD-11 trauma-related disorders (PTSD or CPTSD) was 23.8% (95% CI 12.1-39.5%; n = 10), with PTSD diagnosed in 6 participants (14.3%; 95% CI 5.4-28.5%) and CPTSD in 4 participants (9.5%; 95% CI 2.7-22.6%). No statistically significant associations were found for any of the examined variables. Exploratory subgroup analyses revealed numerically higher rates of trauma-related disorders in patients with prior psychiatric treatment (40.0% vs. 21.6%), ECMO therapy (33.3% vs. 16.7%), or renal replacement therapy (50.0% vs. 17.6%); however, these findings should be interpreted with caution given the limited sample size. Nearly one quarter of COVID-19 ICU survivors met the diagnostic criteria for PTSD or CPTSD, a prevalence comparable to that observed in other critically ill populations. No statistically significant associations were identified, and the observed subgroup differences should be regarded as exploratory and hypothesis-generating. The reported prevalence of PTSD/CPTSD highlights the potential value of systematic screening for trauma-related disorder and the integration of psychological support into post-ICU care. Larger prospective multicenter studies are needed to confirm these findings and further characterize potential risk factors. The study was reviewed and approved by the Ethics committee of the Medical Association of Saarland (Number 98/22).

title: The Relationship Between Political Affiliation, Perceptions of Science and Scientists, and Perceived Safety and Effectiveness of the MMR, Flu, and COVID-19 Vaccines: United States, 2024.
abstract: To examine the associations between political party identification, perceptions of science and scientists, and perceived safety and effectiveness of the measles, mumps, and rubella, flu, and COVID-19 vaccines. We used multiple regression analyses to examine survey data collected in November 2024 from a national probability sample of 1763 US adults. We measured perceptions of science and scientists using the Factors Assessing Science's Self-Presentation (FASS) scale, which assesses beliefs that scientists are credible, prudent, and unbiased and that science is beneficial and self-correcting. Respondents perceived the measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine as the safest and most effective (mean safety score = 3.54 [SD = 0.71]; mean effectiveness score = 3.63 [SD = 0.68]) and the COVID-19 vaccine as the least safe and effective (mean safety score = 2.98 [SD = 1.07]; mean effectiveness score = 2.81 [SD = 1.02]). Republicans are more concerned about the safety and effectiveness of vaccines, with politicization most evident for the COVID-19 vaccine. Public Health Implications. title: Child maltreatment and harsh parenting in Canada during the COVID-19 pandemic: a scoping review of the epidemiological evidence, methodological and data gaps, and recommendations for strengthening public health data.
abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic caused widespread disruptions to social relationships and caregiving responsibilities, potentially modifying risks for child maltreatment (CM) and harsh parenting (HP). However, the impact of the pandemic on the epidemiology of CM and HP is unclear. Objective The objectives of this scoping review were to summarize evidence on the epidemiology of CM and HP in Canada during the COVID-19 pandemic, assess the quality of the included evidence to support the interpretation of the findings, and synthesize published recommendations to strengthen data. Methods We conducted a systematic search of five bibliographic databases and Statistics Canada's website for relevant Canadian studies published between January 1, 2020 and July 4, 2024. We summarized the findings with descriptive statistics and a narrative review, and assessed study quality using an adapted version of the Evidence-Based Social Services Critical Thinking Tool. Results Twenty-seven studies were included; 81.5% reported on CM. Administrative data indicated fewer referrals to child protection services and hospital visits, but increases in police-reported family violence against children. The quality of studies was negatively impacted by non-representative samples, unstandardized measures, and limited use of pre-pandemic baseline data. Conclusions Due to the lack of reliable and continuous data about CM/HP, governments and researchers in Canada collaborated to improve data infrastructure and better understand the pandemic's impact on the health and wellbeing of children and youth. New data sources were developed to enhance the quality of CM/HP measures and support ongoing public health surveillance. Sustained collaboration among interest-holders and continued efforts to strengthen existing data are necessary to assess the pandemic's long-term effects and prepare to monitor the impacts of future public health emergencies.

title: Increased receptor binding capability of the SARS-CoV-2 saltational variant PJ.2.1
abstract: Abstract The recently identified SARS-CoV-2 saltational variant PJ.2.1, a highly mutated descendant of MC.10.1, has achieved rapid intercontinental spread since its detection in May 2026. Here, we show that PJ.2.1 exhibits exceptionally high human ACE2-binding capability, significantly outperforming contemporary variants such as NB.1.8.1, XFG, and BA.3.2.2. However, despite acquiring over 25 spike mutations, PJ.2.1 remains antigenically similar to the circulating JN.1 family and does not display strong humoral immune evasion. Neutralization profiling indicates that PJ.2.1 possesses heightened neutralization sensitivity to human plasma and RBD-targeting antibodies, especially against cryptic-site-targeting class 4 and class 5 antibodies. This distinct sensitivity profile strongly suggests an altered spike structural dynamic that favors a receptor-accessible "up" conformation. While PJ.2.1 currently lacks the extreme immune evasion capabilities of other contemporary strains, its robust baseline receptor binding strength mirrors the early evolutionary trajectory of BA.2.86 to JN.1. This high receptor binding affinity provides a structural buffer that could facilitate the rapid acquisition of potent immune-evasive mutations, necessitating continued genomic, epidemiological, and virological surveillance of PJ.2.1.

title: Healthy vaccinee effect in SARS-CoV-2 vaccinees without documented infection
abstract: Importance: Estimates of SARS-CoV-2 vaccine effectiveness (VE) from observational studies may be biased if healthier (healthy vaccinee effect; HVE) or less healthy individuals are preferentially vaccinated. Quantifying HVE is essential for interpreting VE estimates for informed vaccination policy. Objective: To assess the HVE by comparing all-cause mortality, cancer mortality, and deaths from external causes between vaccinated and unvaccinated individuals. Design, Setting, and Participants: This nationwide retrospective cohort study used Austrian national registry data from 2021 to August 31, 2022, and included the entire adult population of Austria with no previously documented SARS-CoV-2 infection on January 1, 2021. Cox regression was used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) for mortality comparing vaccinated with unvaccinated individuals while adjusting for age, sex and Austrian long-term care allowance (ALTCA) recipiency, stratified by vaccinations (1 to 4). Analyses were performed for the whole observation period, 3-month blocks (quarters) and the 2 months with highest and lowest COVID-19 disease burden per year. Additionally, newly vaccinated individuals were matched on day of vaccination based on the aforementioned covariates plus highest education and HRs were assed for the two weeks following vaccination. Exposure: Receipt of at least 1 dose of SARS-CoV-2 vaccine. Main Outcomes and Measures: All-cause mortality, cancer mortality, and deaths from external causes (e.g., falls and transport accidents). Results: Among 7,416,077 eligible adults, all-cause mortality was lower among vaccinated than unvaccinated individuals regardless of vaccination number. Differences in risk were greatest shortly after vaccination and attenuated over time. E.g., adjusted all-cause HRs in the quarter after vaccination introduction were 0.46, 0.52, 0.38 and 0.43 for vaccinated vs unvaccinated individuals for 1, 2, 3 and 4 vaccinations, respectively. Respective HRs for the first 2 weeks after vaccination in the matched analysis were 0.24-0.32 across all vaccinations. Findings for cancer mortality and deaths from external causes paralleled those for all-cause mortality. Conclusions and Relevance: A pronounced HVE was observed for SARS-CoV-2 vaccination during the pandemic, evidenced by markedly lower mortality from causes not plausibly related to vaccination (cancer, external causes) among vaccinated individuals. This bias needs to be accounted for when interpreting observational estimates of SARS-CoV-2 VE.

source_records.title: Healthy vaccinee effect in SARS-CoV-2 vaccinees without documented infection
source_records.abstract: Importance: Estimates of SARS-CoV-2 vaccine effectiveness (VE) from observational studies may be biased if healthier (healthy vaccinee effect; HVE) or less healthy individuals are preferentially vaccinated. Quantifying HVE is essential for interpreting VE estimates for informed vaccination policy. Objective: To assess the HVE by comparing all-cause mortality, cancer mortality, and deaths from external causes between vaccinated and unvaccinated individuals. Design, Setting, and Participants: This nationwide retrospective cohort study used Austrian national registry data from 2021 to August 31, 2022, and included the entire adult population of Austria with no previously documented SARS-CoV-2 infection on January 1, 2021. Cox regression was used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) for mortality comparing vaccinated with unvaccinated individuals while adjusting for age, sex and Austrian long-term care allowance (ALTCA) recipiency, stratified by vaccinations (1 to 4). Analyses were performed for the whole observation period, 3-month blocks (quarters) and the 2 months with highest and lowest COVID-19 disease burden per year. Additionally, newly vaccinated individuals were matched on day of vaccination based on the aforementioned covariates plus highest education and HRs were assed for the two weeks following vaccination. Exposure: Receipt of at least 1 dose of SARS-CoV-2 vaccine. Main Outcomes and Measures: All-cause mortality, cancer mortality, and deaths from external causes (e.g., falls and transport accidents). Results: Among 7,416,077 eligible adults, all-cause mortality was lower among vaccinated than unvaccinated individuals regardless of vaccination number. Differences in risk were greatest shortly after vaccination and attenuated over time. E.g., adjusted all-cause HRs in the quarter after vaccination introduction were 0.46, 0.52, 0.38 and 0.43 for vaccinated vs unvaccinated individuals for 1, 2, 3 and 4 vaccinations, respectively. Respective HRs for the first 2 weeks after vaccination in the matched analysis were 0.24-0.32 across all vaccinations. Findings for cancer mortality and deaths from external causes paralleled those for all-cause mortality. Conclusions and Relevance: A pronounced HVE was observed for SARS-CoV-2 vaccination during the pandemic, evidenced by markedly lower mortality from causes not plausibly related to vaccination (cancer, external causes) among vaccinated individuals. This bias needs to be accounted for when interpreting observational estimates of SARS-CoV-2 VE.

title: Assessment of the immune response induced by ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 Oxford-AstraZeneca, Sputnik V, and BNT162b2 Pfizer-BioNTech vaccines during the COVID-19 epidemic outbreak in the Mexican population: Gene expression of the cytokine storm.
abstract: COVID-19 vaccines using different technological platforms may induce distinct molecular responses. Characterizing gene-expression patterns after vaccination and in fatal COVID-19 may identify pathways associated with vaccination and severe disease. To compare immune-, inflammatory-, and SARS-CoV-2-entry-related gene expression after AstraZeneca, Pfizer, or Sputnik V vaccination and with unvaccinated fatal COVID-19. Eighty Mexican adults were included: AstraZeneca (n = 19), Pfizer (n = 20), Sputnik (n = 21), and unvaccinated fatal COVID-19 (n = 20). Expression of 11 genes was measured by qPCR at days 30 (D30) and 60 (D60) after vaccination. Longitudinal differences were analyzed by two-way repeated-measures ANOVA. Comparisons with fatal COVID-19 were exploratory. Benjamini-Hochberg correction controlled false discovery rate at 5%. No differences among vaccines were detected at D30. At D60, IL-10, IL-2, and CD79A differed among selected vaccine groups. Longitudinally, FCGR3A decreased in AstraZeneca and Sputnik, ACE2 decreased in Pfizer and Sputnik, and TMPRSS2 increased in Sputnik. Fatal COVID-19 showed predominantly higher expression of several genes than vaccinated groups. Notably, IL-2 and ACE2 were consistently higher in fatal COVID-19 than in all vaccinated groups at both time points. Post-vaccination transcriptional profiles were dynamic, with selected differences emerging at D60, whereas fatal COVID-19 exhibited a distinct profile characterized predominantly by higher expression of immune-, inflammatory-, and viral-entry-related genes. Consistent IL-2 and ACE2 differences highlight molecular pathways potentially associated with severe disease. The observational design, however, precludes causal attribution to vaccination. Longitudinal studies with appropriate controls are needed to establish the biological significance of these transcriptional patterns.

title: Molecular characterization and antifungal susceptibility of Aspergillus spp. isolated from critically ill COVID-19 patients: implications for suspected COVID-19-associated pulmonary aspergillosis (CAPA) in a Brazilian tertiary referral hospital.
abstract: COVID-19-associated pulmonary aspergillosis (CAPA) is a severe complication in critically ill patients, but species identification and antifungal resistance data from middle-income countries remain limited. We analyzed 17 Aspergillus isolates from respiratory specimens of 15 critically ill patients with COVID-19 in São Paulo State, Brazil, during 2020-2021. Patients were retrospectively classified according to ECMM/ISHAM criteria as probable CAPA (n = 5), possible CAPA (n = 7), or non-CAPA (n = 3). Complementary reassessment using the 2024 FUNDICU definitions classified patients as probable invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA; n = 3), probable tracheobronchial aspergillosis (TBA; n = 1), or as not meeting these definitions (n = 9); two were ineligible due to classical EORTC/MSGERC host factors (n = 2). Species identification was performed by benA sequencing and MALDI-TOF MS. Susceptibility to amphotericin B (AMB), itraconazole (ITZ), voriconazole (VCZ), and posaconazole (PCZ) was determined according to CLSI M38-A2, and cyp51A and its promoter were analyzed in A. The predominant species were A. fumigatus (n = 7) and A. flavus (n = 5), followed by A. welwitschiae (n = 1 each). fumigatus isolates exhibited non-wild-type phenotypes (NWT) against PCZ, with some also showing reduced susceptibility to ITZ and AMB. Silent cyp51A mutations occurred in three A. fumigatus isolates, while several section Flavi isolates displayed multiazole NWT. These findings highlight diagnostic limitations and emerging azole resistance, supporting susceptibility testing and surveillance.

title: Isolation and Quarantine Policies During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Narrative Review on Global Challenges, Implementation Barriers, and Lessons Learned
abstract: Isolation, quarantine, and contact tracing are some of the most critical and commonly employed non-pharmaceutical interventions used to control the spread of COVID-19. However, the effectiveness of these strategies and their implementation depends on many factors, including a country’s population, the availability of resources to diagnose and effectively isolate infected individuals, culture and societal beliefs, family dynamics, and the feasibility and acceptability of isolation and quarantine policies among the public. This narrative review aims to appraise the evidence on the implementation strategies and shortcomings of isolation and quarantine strategies adopted during the COVID-19 pandemic. Previous evidence has found that early quarantine and isolation of COVID-19 patients were more effective than late adoption (5-fold vs. Approximately 90% of outbreaks could have been managed if 80% of contacts were monitored, traced, and isolated within four days of the index case being identified. For each new case of COVID-19, around thirty-six individuals should be traced. When the percentage of asymptomatic individuals is greater than 30%, isolation and contact tracing alone cannot contain the infection. The delay between symptom onset and isolation was the most important factor in determining infection control. Symptom-based isolation strategies should not be considered the sole criterion for isolation, as many asymptomatic individuals escaped isolation and increased the risk of disease transmission. Digital contact tracing, telemedicine, and artificial intelligence (AI)-based surveillance systems are potential adjuncts to support isolation and quarantine measures. Changes in societal behaviors and cultural norms, fear of stigma, psychological issues, economic burden, poverty, poor literacy rates, lack of public trust in government, and language were identified as challenges and barriers associated with the effective implementation of isolation and quarantine measures during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Fear of death increases nocebo-prone behavior in people with headaches during covid-19. A longitudinal observational survey.
abstract: BACKGROUND The nocebo effect greatly affects pain management. We investigated the nocebo-prone behavior in people with headaches during and after the COVID-19 pandemic, for which there is clear evidence that the nocebo effect increased. METHODS Individuals with headaches completed a series of questionnaires, including the Q-No, MIDAS, HIT-6, fear of death because of COVID-19 (a questionnaire including levels from 0 = no fear, to 3 = intense fear of death), and Hamilton Anxiety and Depression Rating Scale, over three consecutive periods. Period A was characterized by prolonged lockdowns, period B by strict pandemic regulations, and period C by the lifting of containment measures. RESULTS 212 participants, 151 (71.2%) completed assessments across all three periods and were included. Nocebo-prone behavior (Q-No score ≥ 15) was detected in 16.6%, 14% and 9% of 151 participants in Period A, B and C, respectively (p < 0.05). Fear of death due to COVID-19 was recorded by 27.8%, 23.2% and 15.2%. Nocebo-prone behavior was independently associated with fear of death, anxiety symptoms, monthly headache days and HIT-6 score. CONCLUSION Nocebo-prone behavior in individuals with headache appears to be dynamic and associated with psychological and clinical burden. Targeted, personalized interventions addressing fear, anxiety, and headache burden may mitigate nocebo effects and optimize headache management.

title: Correlation assessment of SARS-CoV-2 variants and their subvariants present in clinical and wastewater samples in Oregon, USA (February 7, 2021 - February 26, 2022) using the Freyja bioinformatics approach.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Wastewater surveillance is a valuable tool for monitoring SARS-CoV-2 at the community level. As the virus diversified into many variants and subvariants that share overlapping mutations, resolving them accurately from wastewater becomes a key bioinformatic challenge. OBJECTIVES AND AIMS: This study evaluated two distinct bioinformatic approaches, multilocus sequence typing (MLST) and Freyja, for identifying SARS-CoV-2 variants and subvariants in Oregon wastewater samples collected from February 2021 to February 2022. METHODS: The MLST approach identified SARS-CoV-2 variants using unique mutations curated from clinical samples. In contrast, the Freyja approach resolved variant and subvariant abundances using genome wide mutation profiles weighted by sequencing depth. In this study, the variant and subvariants relative abundances produced by both approaches were compared against those observed in clinical surveillance data. RESULTS: Both approaches identified SARS-CoV-2 variants at relative abundances that agreed closely with those observed in clinical surveillance data. However, only the Freyja approach identified over 200 Delta subvariants, divided into three clades (21A, 21I and 21J) and two levels (Level 1 and 2) based on Pango subvariants. Delta subvariants showed strong agreement at Level 1 subvariants (rs = 0.892-0.944), while agreement at Level 2 subvariants was inconsistent (rs = 0.324-0.903). CONCLUSIONS: The Freyja approach provided enhanced resolution of SARS-CoV-2 variants and subvariants in wastewater, at abundances that agreed with clinical surveillance. This added resolution is a critical advantage for public health surveillance as SARS-CoV-2 continues to evolve and share mutations across variants and subvariants.

Objectives and aims This study evaluated two distinct bioinformatic approaches, multilocus sequence typing (MLST) and Freyja, for identifying SARS-CoV-2 variants and subvariants in Oregon wastewater samples collected from February 2021 to February 2022. Methods The MLST approach identified SARS-CoV-2 variants using unique mutations curated from clinical samples. In contrast, the Freyja approach resolved variant and subvariant abundances using genome wide mutation profiles weighted by sequencing depth. In this study, the variant and subvariants relative abundances produced by both approaches were compared against those observed in clinical surveillance data. Results Both approaches identified SARS-CoV-2 variants at relative abundances that agreed closely with those observed in clinical surveillance data. However, only the Freyja approach identified over 200 Delta subvariants, divided into three clades (21A, 21I and 21J) and two levels (Level 1 and 2) based on Pango subvariants. Delta subvariants showed strong agreement at Level 1 subvariants (rs = 0.892-0.944), while agreement at Level 2 subvariants was inconsistent (rs = 0.324-0.903). Conclusions The Freyja approach provided enhanced resolution of SARS-CoV-2 variants and subvariants in wastewater, at abundances that agreed with clinical surveillance. This added resolution is a critical advantage for public health surveillance as SARS-CoV-2 continues to evolve and share mutations across variants and subvariants.
